items.title: CENTCOM denies Iran's claim of missile strike as Hormuz operation begins

featured_image.name: Iran fires missiles into Strait of Hormuz during military exercise as  nuclear talks begin | The Times of Israel

items.description: Iran said on Monday that it struck a U.S. Navy frigate with two missiles near the Strait of Hormuz, a claim swiftly denied by the U.S. military as President Donald Trump's high-stakes naval operation to reopen the waterway got underway. The dueling narratives underscored the volatility of a standoff that has choked off roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas shipments for more than two months.

items.title: Two US-flagged ships transit Hormuz under Project Freedom

featured_image.name: US and allied naval commanders in Mideast transit Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
Two U.S.-flagged merchant vessels successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday under the Trump administration's "Project Freedom" initiative, marking the first publicly acknowledged American-backed passage through the strategic waterway since Iran imposed a blockade more than two months ago.

"American forces are actively assisting efforts to restore transit for commercial shipping. As a first step, two U.S.-flagged merchant vessels have successfully transited through the Strait of Hormuz and are safely headed on their journey," U.S. Central Command said in a post on X.[1][2]

CENTCOM confirmed that U.S. Navy guided-missile destroyers entered the Arabian Gulf after transiting the strait in support of the operation. The mission involves approximately 15,000 service members, more than 100 land- and sea-based aircraft, and unmanned platforms across multiple domains.[3][4][1]

items.title: Iran fires missiles at US warship as Project Freedom launches

featured_image.name: Iran-US war latest: Tehran 'hits US warship with two missiles' in Strait of  Hormuz after issuing warning to Trump | The Independent

items.description:
Two Iranian missiles struck a U.S. warship near Iran's Jask Island on Monday after the vessel reportedly ignored Iranian warnings while attempting to enter the Strait of Hormuz, according to IRGC-affiliated Fars News. The reported strike came just hours after U.S. Central Command began Project Freedom, the American military operation to escort stranded commercial vessels through the contested waterway.[1][2]

Oil prices surged on the news, reflecting the market's acute sensitivity to military confrontations in the corridor through which roughly a quarter of the world's seaborne oil trade passes. Brent crude had already been trading above $116 per barrel heading into the week.[3][4][5]

items.title: Iran vows to attack US forces as Project Freedom launches in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: US will help 'guide' trapped ships out of the Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Sunday announced a naval operation called "Project Freedom" to guide stranded commercial ships through the blocked Strait of Hormuz, setting up a direct confrontation with Iran, which warned it would attack any foreign military force entering the waterway.

The operation, revealed in a Truth Social post, is set to begin Monday morning Middle East time. Trump described the stranded vessels as belonging to countries that are "neutral and innocent bystanders" with no involvement in the broader Middle East conflict. "For the good of Iran, the Middle East, and the United States, we have told these Countries that we will guide their Ships safely out of these restricted Waterways," Trump wrote.[1][2][3]

items.title: Cargo ship attacked near Strait of Hormuz as peace talks stall

featured_image.name: Cargo ship near Strait of Hormuz reports attack as Iran makes new peace proposal

items.description:
A bulk carrier near the Strait of Hormuz reported being attacked by multiple small craft on Sunday, according to the British military's United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center, marking at least the 24th attack in and around the vital waterway since the Iran war began in late February.[1][2]

The UKMTO said the northbound vessel was attacked 11 nautical miles west of Sirik, Iran, east of the strait, and that all crew were safe. No one immediately claimed responsibility for the incident, the first reported in the area since April 22. The threat level in the region remains classified as critical.[3][2]
